review_notes: I read the whole target file (two theorems). The second theorem is a thin wrapper around the first, and its `nlinarith` step is a short calculation, so neither is a finding. I grepped for the other uses of `boundedColumnResidueRepresentative_bounds` and read the sites in AllocatedReferenceJetMass.lean (lines 242 and 345), AllocatedLocalResidueReconstruction.lean, SelectedResidueRefinementMean.lean and AllocatedPositiveSpatialComparison.lean. The one repeated pattern is the cast of `0 ≤ r < q` to ℝ and the resulting `|(r : ℝ)| ≤ q` bound. Each copy is only 3–5 lines, so the finding is a modest one. No existing lemma with that statement turned up in my search for `boundedColumnResidueRepresentative_abs`, `_real` or `_cast`. I did not compile anything, and the shared lemma name below is a proposal.

findings.excerpt: obtain ⟨h0, h1⟩ := boundedColumnResidueRepresentative_bounds q hq a i
findings.problem: The proof turns the integer facts `0 ≤ r` and `r < q` into the real facts `0 ≤ (r : ℝ)` and `(r : ℝ) < q` by hand. Then it applies `abs_of_nonneg` to get `|(r : ℝ)| ≤ q`. The same cast-and-abs argument, with only the index names changed, is copied in at least six other places. These include AllocatedReferenceJetMass.lean (two `hr` blocks, around lines 240–244 and 343–347), AllocatedLocalResidueReconstruction.lean (around lines 582 and 676), SelectedResidueRefinementMean.lean (around line 146) and AllocatedPositiveSpatialComparison.lean (around lines 69 and 268). Every copy re-derives the same real-valued bound from the integer lemma.
findings.proposed_change: Next to `boundedColumnResidueRepresentative_bounds` in SelectedResidueApproximation.lean, add a lemma with the same hypotheses and the conclusion `0 ≤ (boundedColumnResidueRepresentative modulus r z : ℝ) ∧ (boundedColumnResidueRepresentative modulus r z : ℝ) < (modulus z.2 : ℝ)`, and perhaps a second one stating `|(… : ℝ)| ≤ modulus z.2`. The proof is `obtain ⟨h0, h1⟩ := boundedColumnResidueRepresentative_bounds modulus hmodulus r z`, then `exact_mod_cast` on each part, then `abs_of_nonneg` for the absolute-value form. In the target, `hsmall` then starts from `0 ≤ (z i : ℝ)` and `(z i : ℝ) < q i.2` directly, and the `hz`/`hzq` casts disappear. The `hr` blocks in AllocatedReferenceJetMass.lean and AllocatedLocalResidueReconstruction.lean become a single application of the abs lemma. The blocks in SelectedResidueRefinementMean.lean and AllocatedPositiveSpatialComparison.lean also drop their `hr0` cast.
findings.benefit: The integer-to-real cast of the representative bounds lives in one place. Readers no longer have to re-check the same cast-and-abs steps in each proof. A later change to the representative's definition or bounds statement only needs one proof updated.
